title: Adding and subtracting coplanar vectors practice

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: direct Lesson 9 retrieval, head-to-tail construction, collinear cancellation, subtraction by reversal, perpendicular addition, numerical vector subtraction, then a mixed three-vector route using Lesson 9 reporting knowledge

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, values, wording and figure briefs are newly authored. The repaired four-leaf P2 evidence set grounds head-to-tail diagrams, opposite-collinear subtraction and perpendicular resultant magnitude. Component-resolution leaves from the same whole-question contexts are deliberately excluded.

questions.prompt: From Lesson 9, state what is meant by a vector quantity and state what must be included in a complete numerical report of a vector.
Which description gives the correct construction for adding vector A to vector B?

options.A: Place the tail of B at the head of A, then draw the resultant from the tail of A to the head of B.
options.B: Place both tails together, then draw the resultant from the head of A to the head of B.
options.C: Reverse B, place its tail at the head of A, then join the start to the finish.
options.D: Add the two magnitudes and draw the answer in the direction of A.

questions.prompt: Two forces of 14 N east and 9 N west act along the same line. What is their resultant?
Which operation correctly represents $\vec{A}-\vec{B}$ on a vector diagram?

options.A: Reverse A and add B head-to-tail.
options.B: Reverse B and add the reversed vector to A head-to-tail.
options.C: Keep both directions and subtract only their drawn lengths.
options.D: Place both heads together and add their magnitudes.

questions.prompt: A hiker walks 12 km east and then 5.0 km north.

figure.purpose: Provide a clean drawing area and compass reference for a head-to-tail resultant construction without revealing the resultant.
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular line diagram. Show a start dot near the lower left, a small north-east compass and a light square grid. Give the scale 1 square represents 1 km. Do not draw either journey vector, the resultant, a triangle or an angle.
figure.alt_text: A blank square grid with a start point, compass directions and a scale of one square per kilometre.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: On the grid, draw the two displacement vectors head-to-tail and draw and label their resultant R.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the direction of R, measured north of east.

questions.prompt: Vector A is 7.0 m east. Vector B is 3.0 m north. Determine $\vec{A}-\vec{B}$.

figure.purpose: Show the two given vectors clearly while leaving the reversal, head-to-tail construction and resultant for the learner.
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular vector diagram. From one origin draw A as a 7.0 m east arrow and B as a 3.0 m north arrow. Include sparse labels and a north-east compass. Leave wide blank space to the east and south. Do not draw minus B, the resultant, an angle or any answer value.
figure.alt_text: Vector A points 7.0 metres east and vector B points 3.0 metres north from a common origin.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Draw a head-to-tail construction for $\vec{A}-\vec{B}$ and label the resultant R.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the direction of R, measured from east.

questions.prompt: A survey robot moves for 48 s. It travels 9.0 m west, then 12 m south, and finally 4.0 m east.

figure.purpose: Support a three-vector route construction while keeping the resultant and all calculations learner-generated.
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular square grid with a marked start point and a north-east compass. State a scale of 1 square represents 1 m. Leave the route, final point, resultant and angle entirely blank.
figure.alt_text: A blank square grid with a start point and compass for drawing a three-stage robot route.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using Lesson 9 knowledge, classify the time and each displacement as scalar or vector quantities, and explain the distinction.

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (c)
